```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(apa7)
library(metafor)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
#| label: setup2
#| eval: false
<<setup>>
```

`apa_parameters` and `apa_performance` make APA-style tables of meta-analyses fit with `metafor::rma`:

| Table | Function | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| Studies and pooled estimate | `apa_parameters` | Each study's effect size, confidence interval, and weight, followed by the pooled estimate |
| Meta-regression | `apa_parameters` | Coefficients of the moderators, as for other regression models |
| Heterogeneity | `apa_performance` | *k*, *Q*, *&tau;*^2^, *I*^2^, and, for meta-regressions, the test of the moderators and *R*^2^ |
| Subgroups | `apa_subgroups` | Each subgroup's pooled estimate and the test of subgroup differences |
| Publication bias | `apa_publication_bias` | Egger's regression test, the rank correlation test, and trim and fill, with adjusted estimates |

# Studies and the Pooled Estimate

The `dat.molloy2014` data set in the metadat package (installed with metafor) has the correlations between conscientiousness and medication adherence in 16 studies. Correlations are meta-analyzed as Fisher's *z* values (`measure = "ZCOR"` in `escalc`), and `slab` gives the study labels:

```{r}
#| label: molloy
d_adherence <- escalc(
  measure = "ZCOR",
  ri = ri,
  ni = ni,
  data = metadat::dat.molloy2014,
  slab = paste(authors, year)
)

fit_adherence <- rma(yi, vi, data = d_adherence)

apa_parameters(fit_adherence) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)
```

Each study's correlation and confidence interval, and the pooled estimate below the rule, are converted back from Fisher's *z* to *r*. The weights are each study's percentage of the total weight in the random-effects model. The note names the measure and the model, and it gives the test of the pooled estimate, its 95% prediction interval (the range in which the true effect of a new study is expected to fall), and the test of heterogeneity.

The column of effect sizes is named by the measure given to `escalc`: for example, *g* for standardized mean differences (`"SMD"`), *r* for correlations (`"COR"` or `"ZCOR"`), and *OR*, *RR*, or *IRR* for odds ratios, risk ratios, and incidence rate ratios. Ratios are analyzed on the log scale and exponentiated for the table. With `transform = FALSE`, estimates stay on the scale on which they were analyzed (e.g., log risk ratios). With `weights = FALSE`, the weights are left out.

# Heterogeneity

`apa_performance` gives the heterogeneity statistics:

```{r}
#| label: molloy-heterogeneity
apa_performance(fit_adherence) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)
```

With `metrics = "all"`, the table adds *&tau;*, *H*^2^, and confidence intervals of *&tau;*^2^ and *I*^2^.

# Ratio Measures

In the `dat.bcg` data set, 13 trials compared the risk of tuberculosis in people who were and were not vaccinated with BCG. The effect sizes are risk ratios, which are analyzed on the log scale and exponentiated for the table:

```{r}
#| label: bcg
d_bcg <- escalc(
  measure = "RR",
  ai = tpos, bi = tneg, ci = cpos, di = cneg,
  data = metadat::dat.bcg,
  slab = paste(author, year)
) |> 
  rename(Latitude = ablat,
         Allocation = alloc) |> 
  mutate(Allocation = factor(stringr::str_to_title(Allocation)))


fit_bcg <- rma(yi, vi, data = d_bcg)

apa_parameters(fit_bcg) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)
```

# Meta-Regression

Moderators are added with `mods`. The vaccine appeared to work better in trials farther from the equator, so here the absolute latitude of each trial is a moderator:

```{r}
#| label: bcg-metareg
fit_latitude <- rma(yi, vi, mods = ~ Latitude, data = d_bcg)

apa_parameters(fit_latitude) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)

apa_performance(fit_latitude) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)
```

For a meta-regression, `apa_parameters` shows the intercept and moderators, as for other regression models. Coefficients (*B*) are on the scale on which the effect sizes were analyzed (here, log risk ratios), and for ratio measures, the exponentiated coefficients are added (here, *RR*): each degree of latitude multiplies the risk ratio by about 0.97. `apa_performance` adds the omnibus test of the moderators (*Q*~M~) and the percentage of heterogeneity they explain (*R*^2^), and *Q*~E~ is the test of the heterogeneity that remains.

# Subgroup Analysis

A subgroup analysis compares the pooled estimates of groups of studies. In the BCG trials, participants were assigned to the vaccine at random, alternately, or systematically. `apa_subgroups` pools each group of trials and compares them:

```{r}
#| label: subgroups
apa_subgroups(fit_bcg, Allocation) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)
```

By default, each subgroup has its own *&tau;*^2^, and the subgroups are compared with *Q*~between~, the heterogeneity of the subgroup estimates. With `tau2 = "common"`, the subgroups share one *&tau;*^2^, which is estimated more precisely when subgroups have few studies: the estimates come from a meta-regression with the subgroup as a categorical moderator, and the subgroups are compared with its omnibus test (*Q*~M~). The subgroup variable can be a column of the data (quoted or unquoted) or a vector (e.g., `d_bcg$Latititude > 30`).

# Publication Bias

`apa_publication_bias` tests for publication bias (small-study effects) and gives estimates adjusted for it, as computed by metafor: Egger's regression test, with its limit estimate (the predicted effect of a study with a standard error of zero); Begg and Mazumdar's rank correlation test; and trim and fill, with the number of studies it imputed (*k*~0~) and the pooled estimate with them included:

```{r}
#| label: publication-bias
apa_publication_bias(fit_adherence) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)
```

The adjusted estimates are on the same scale as the table of studies (here, correlations), and the note gives the unadjusted pooled estimate for comparison. Add `"fsn"` to `methods` for the fail-safe *N*, which is widely criticized and is not shown by default. These methods are available for `rma` models without moderators.

# Multilevel Meta-Analysis

When studies report several effect sizes, the effect sizes are not independent, and a multilevel (three-level) model with `rma.mv` has a random intercept for each level. In the `dat.konstantopoulos2011` data set, 56 schools in 11 school districts compared the achievement of students on modified and traditional school calendars (standardized mean differences). The table of a multilevel model has a row for each effect size, so this example shows only the pooled estimate (`studies = FALSE`):

```{r}
#| label: multilevel
fit_schools <- rma.mv(
  yi, vi,
  random = ~ 1 | district / school,
  data = metadat::dat.konstantopoulos2011
)

apa_parameters(fit_schools, studies = FALSE) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)

apa_performance(fit_schools) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)
```

`apa_performance` gives the variance of the true effects at each level (*&sigma;*^2^, with the level as a subscript) and the multilevel *I*^2^ (Cheung, 2014), the percentage of the total variability due to heterogeneity at all levels. With `metrics = "all"`, the table adds *&sigma;* and confidence intervals of *&sigma;*^2^ for each level, and *I*^2^ for each level. Meta-regressions of multilevel models work as for `rma`. Random effects with an `~ inner | outer` structure (e.g., correlated outcomes within studies) are not yet supported.

# Citations in Notes

Some notes cite the articles that describe a method (e.g., trim and fill and the multilevel *I*^2^). In the console and in this article, the citations are written as text. To have them formatted and added to the reference list of a Quarto or R Markdown document, see [Citations in notes](regression.html#citations-in-notes) in the regression article.

# Options

* `method = "EE"` in `rma` fits an equal-effects model; the table labels the pooled estimate accordingly, and there is no prediction interval or *&tau;*^2^.
* `test = "knha"` in `rma` uses the Knapp–Hartung adjustment; the pooled estimate is tested with *t*, and the note says so.
* `studies = FALSE` shows only the pooled estimate, with its test, instead of the study rows.
* Multilevel models with random intercepts (`rma.mv` with `random = ~ 1 | study / effect`) are supported; random effects with an `~ inner | outer` structure are not yet supported.
